text_blocks.snippet: Treatment for type 2 diabetes involves managing blood glucose levels through healthy lifestyle changes, oral or injectable medications, and regular monitoring.

list.snippet: Healthy diet: Focus on whole grains, lean proteins, non-starchy vegetables, and healthy fats while reducing high-sugar foods and refined carbs.
Regular exercise: Aim for at least 30 minutes of physical activity daily to help lower blood sugar and promote weight loss.
Weight management: Reaching and maintaining a healthy weight improves the body's response to insulin.
Metformin: The most common first-line oral medication, which decreases glucose production in the liver and improves insulin sensitivity.
Other oral medications: Includes sulfonylureas (boost insulin production), DPP-4 inhibitors, SGLT2 inhibitors (help excrete sugar via urine), and thiazolidinediones.
Injectable medications: Includes GLP-1 receptor agonists (which also help with weight management and heart health).
Insulin therapy: Used when other medications and lifestyle habits do not sufficiently control blood sugar. It can be administered via pens, syringes, or pumps.
Blood glucose tracking: Checking levels regularly using a standard glucometer or a continuous glucose monitor (CGM).
Coexisting conditions: Managing blood pressure and cholesterol levels to prevent long-term cardiovascular and kidney complications.
